mangal.mantra1: Om. Salutations to the Supreme Self.
mangal.shloka1: O Lord with the curved trunk and mighty body, radiant as millions of suns: keep all my undertakings free of obstacles, always.
mangal.shloka2: To the Lord of obstacles, the giver of boons, beloved of the gods; to the large-bellied one, complete in every part, who works the good of the world; to the elephant-faced one, adorned by the Vedas and sacrifices; to the son of Gaurī: O Lord of the gaṇas, salutations to you again and again.
mangal.mantra2: Om. Salutations to the Supreme Self.
chalisa.do1: Having cleansed the mirror of my mind with the dust of my revered Guru's lotus feet, I describe the spotless glory of Śrī Rāma, best of the Raghus, which bestows the four fruits of life (dharma, wealth, desire and liberation).
chalisa.do2: Knowing myself to be devoid of intelligence, I remember you, O son of the Wind. Grant me strength, intelligence and knowledge, and take away my afflictions and impurities.
chalisa.cau1: Glory to you, Hanumān, ocean of wisdom and virtue! Glory to you, lord of the monkeys, renowned in all three worlds!
chalisa.cau2: You are Śrī Rāma's messenger, the abode of matchless strength, known by the names Añjanī's son and son of the Wind.
chalisa.cau3: O great hero, mighty in valour, with limbs hard as a thunderbolt, you dispel evil thoughts and are the companion of those whose minds are good.
chalisa.cau4: Golden in hue, you shine in fine attire, with earrings in your ears and curly hair.
chalisa.cau5: In your hands shine the thunderbolt and the banner, and a sacred thread of muñja grass adorns your shoulder.
chalisa.cau6: Born of Śaṅkara, son of Kesarī, your splendour and might are great, and the whole world worships you.
chalisa.cau7: Learned, virtuous and exceedingly wise, you are ever eager to do Śrī Rāma's work.
chalisa.cau8: You delight in hearing the Lord's story; Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā dwell in your heart.
chalisa.cau9: Taking a tiny form, you showed yourself to Sītā; taking a formidable form, you burnt Laṅkā.
chalisa.cau10: Taking a terrible form, you slew the demons and accomplished Śrī Rāmacandra's tasks.
chalisa.cau11: You brought the life-giving herb and revived Lakṣmaṇa, and Śrī Raghuvīra joyfully clasped you to his heart.
chalisa.cau12: The lord of the Raghus praised you greatly: 'You are as dear to me as my brother Bharata.'
chalisa.cau13: 'The thousand-mouthed Śeṣa sings your glory,' said the consort of Lakṣmī, and embraced you.
chalisa.cau14: Sanaka and the other sages, Brahmā and the other gods, the great sages, Nārada, Sarasvatī and Śeṣa, the lord of serpents (sing your glory).
chalisa.cau15: When Yama, Kubera and the guardians of the quarters cannot tell it fully, how could poets and scholars?
chalisa.cau16: You did Sugrīva a great favour: you brought him to Rāma and gave him the kingdom.
chalisa.cau17: Vibhīṣaṇa heeded your counsel and became the king of Laṅkā; the whole world knows it.
chalisa.cau18: The sun, thousands of yojanas away, you swallowed, taking it for a sweet fruit.
chalisa.cau19: Holding the Lord's ring in your mouth, you leapt across the ocean; no wonder in that.
chalisa.cau20: However many hard tasks there are in the world, all become easy by your grace.
chalisa.cau21: You are the guardian of Rāma's door; no one enters there without your leave.
chalisa.cau22: Whoever takes refuge in you finds every joy; with you as protector, there is nothing to fear.
chalisa.cau23: You alone can contain your own splendour; the three worlds tremble at your roar.
chalisa.cau24: Ghosts and demons do not come near when the name of the great hero is uttered.
chalisa.cau25: Disease is destroyed and all pain removed by ceaselessly repeating the name of the brave Hanumān.
chalisa.cau26: Hanumān frees from distress whoever fixes their meditation on him in thought, word and deed.
chalisa.cau27: Rāma, the ascetic king, is supreme over all, and you accomplished all his tasks.
chalisa.cau28: Whoever comes with any other wish obtains its fruit without limit in this life.
chalisa.cau29: Your glory spreads through all four ages, famed as a light across the world.
chalisa.cau30: You are the protector of saints and holy men, the destroyer of demons, the darling of Rāma.
chalisa.cau31: Mother Jānakī granted you the boon of being the giver of the eight siddhis and the nine treasures.
chalisa.cau32: You hold the elixir of Rāma('s name); may you ever remain the servant of the lord of the Raghus.
chalisa.cau33: Through devotion to you one attains Rāma and leaves behind the sorrows of birth after birth.
chalisa.cau34: At the end one goes to the city of Rāma, and wherever one is born, is called a devotee of Hari.
chalisa.cau35: Even without holding any other deity in mind, one who serves Hanumān gains every joy.
chalisa.cau36: Troubles are cut away and all pain removed for whoever remembers the mighty hero Hanumān.
chalisa.cau37: Glory, glory, glory to you, Lord Hanumān! Be gracious to me as my Guru is.
chalisa.cau38: Whoever recites this a hundred times is released from bondage and finds great joy.
chalisa.cau39: Whoever reads this Hanumān Chālīsā attains success; Śiva, lord of Gaurī, is witness to it.
chalisa.cau40: Tulasīdāsa is ever Hari's servant; O Lord, make your dwelling in my heart.
chalisa.do3: O son of the Wind, remover of troubles, embodiment of auspiciousness, king of the gods: dwell in my heart together with Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa and Sītā.
aarti.tek: Perform the āratī of Hanumān, the darling son (of Añjanā), crusher of the wicked, a portion of Śrī Rāma's own power.
aarti.pad1: By his strength the great mountains tremble; disease and fault dare not come near him. Añjanā's son is the giver of great strength, the lord who ever helps the saints.
aarti.pad2: Śrī Rāma gave him the betel roll of the task and sent him; he burnt Laṅkā and brought news of Sītā. Laṅkā had a fortress and a moat like the ocean, yet the son of the Wind went without delay.
aarti.pad3: He burnt Laṅkā, slew the demons and accomplished the tasks of Sītā and Rāma. When Lakṣmaṇa lay unconscious, he brought the life-restoring herb before daybreak and saved his life.
aarti.pad4: Entering the netherworld and breaking through Yama-like guards, he tore off Ahirāvaṇa's arms. With his left arm he slew the demon hosts, with his right he saved the saints.
aarti.pad5: Gods, men and sages wave the āratī and proclaim 'Glory, glory, glory to Hanumān!' The camphor flame spreads over the golden platter as Mother Añjanā performs the āratī.
aarti.pad6: Whoever sings Hanumān's āratī dwells in Vaikuṇṭha and attains the supreme state. Śrī Rāma destroyed Laṅkā, and Tulasīdāsa sang the glory of his Lord.
